body:
Concentrated triage round: `finding` → `pm:queue`, Task, `domain:ui` stands. Zero-reader published type (`MobileComponentConfig`: four mentions, all barrels/self-references) — retire via the ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove route, following the #4919 (`MobileOverrides`) retirement pattern: removal PR with the zero-reader measurement in the body, tombstone per the playbook, both barrels. If the retirement route demands a ledger verdict or turns up a real consumer the census missed, stop and report — do not force the removal.

One line each, nothing else touched in either file.

FOURTH EDIT, IN SCOPE: mobile.ts:50's `{@link MobileComponentConfig}` doc cross-reference (one of the card's own four mentions) is rewritten rather than left dangling at a removed name -- the sentence it formed ('It is consumed only by MobileComponentConfig') would otherwise be false.

If you kept a local config object annotated with it, drop the annotation; the object was never passed anywhere that read it.' / '**You actually wanted the behaviour:** it exists, and it is not being retired. It lives in `@object-ui/mobile` as React hooks, which is where the working code always was -- `useResponsive` / `ResponsiveContainer` for `responsive`, `useGesture` for `gestures`, `usePullToRefresh` for `pullToRefresh`. `infiniteScroll` has no hook; it was never implemented in any form. See `skills/objectui/guides/mobile.md`.' / '**You want a declarative mobile config surface:** that re-enters deliberately as designed product surface on its own card, with the renderer that reads it landing in the same change as the declaration -- not by restoring this declaration.' It also states 'No behaviour changes and there is nothing to migrate at runtime' and 'Breaking for TypeScript consumers of the name only'.

CONSEQUENCE, NOT WIDENED: MobileComponentConfig was the SOLE consumer of two other published types on the same file -- MobileResponsiveConfig (:285) and GestureConfig (:287). Both become zero-consumer published types after this change; visible in the dist controls (MobileResponsiveConfig 4 hits -> 3, GestureConfig 7 -> 6, each losing exactly its mount point). Filed as #7519 rather than fixed here, for the same reason #5941 filed this card: MobileResponsiveConfig carries a spec name-ownership tripwire (page-nav-misc-spec-parity.test.ts:749) that outlives the type, and retire-vs-implement is a product call. Their live siblings GestureType / GestureContext / ResponsiveValue ARE genuinely read (useGesture.ts, useSpecGesture.ts, breakpoints.ts, useResponsive.ts) and are untouched.

PR is draft with needs:contract-review on BOTH carriers (PR #7526 label added and read back = ['needs:contract-review']; card side was already set by PM).
